title: Cortex-specific inversion of visual responses during sleep
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-73997-y

While we sleep, we disengage from the external environment. Using EEG-fMRI, we found that during sleep visual signals reach the thalamus but are suppressed in the visual cortex, revealing a cortical mechanism that isolates our senses during sleep.

title: Low-hygroscopic solvents enable ambient blade coating of efficient perovskite solar cells
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-72581-8

Scalable perovskite solar cell production is limited by moisture sensitive interfacial layers. Li et al. develop a low hygroscopic solvent system enabling ambient blade coating of precursors, including self-assembled monolayers and passivation layers, yielding high device efficiency.

title: Nationwide spread of multidrug resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae across US communities
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74379-0

A nationwide genomic survey of outpatient isolates from 42 US states reveals a rapidly spreading, plasmid-driven epidemic of multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae, largely driven by the dissemination of blaCTX-M-15 plasmids across US communities.

title: Light-triggered oxygen redox activity at the edge of cobalt oxyhydroxide for superior water oxidation
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74386-1

Light-driven oxygen redox offers a new strategy to boost oxygen evolution activity by enabling direct O–O bond formation. Here, the authors report that sulfur-treated cobalt oxyhydroxide generates non-bonding oxygen states under light, enhancing oxygen evolution performance.

title: Targeted next-generation sequencing implementation in Eswatini identifies rifampicin and bedaquiline resistance undetected by routine diagnostic testing
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-73551-w

Routine diagnostic tests in Eswatini miss Mycobacterium tuberculosis resistance to key drugs. Here the authors show that targeted next-generation sequencing identifies these elusive strains, guiding personalized treatment and achieving an 88% treatment success rate.

title: Controls on natural hydrogen generation during serpentinization of mantle rocks
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 11 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-73920-5

Natural hydrogen generation during mantle rock serpentinization is slow, limited by fluid saturation and reaction kinetics, suggesting large accumulations require millennia to develop.

title: Stabilizing–sensing synergistic geogrid for high-speed railways
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74260-0

The authors report a stabilizing–sensing geogrid that enhances trackbed stability while enabling integrated fiber-optic monitoring. Full-scale railway loading tests, supported by machine learning, demonstrate durable monitoring and accurate foreign-object detection.

title: GATHeR: graph-based accurate tool for immunoglobulin heavy- and light-chain reconstruction
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 10 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74272-w

Single cell RNA sequencing expanded the possibilities of capturing immune repertoires in lymphocytes but assembling long sequences from the individual reads, especially in naive and memory B cells with low expression of immunoglobulin transcripts is challenging. Here the authors present a computational tool to assemble and annotate paired heavy- and light-chain B-cell receptor sequences which allows distinction of notoriously hard-to-capture splice variants and membrane-bound isoforms.
